key_findings: Qwen3-1.7B 学生 5 数学基准 AVG：本方法 40.1% vs 全序列 OPD 36.8%（+3.3pp），vs 最优固定前缀 OPD 39.4%（+0.7pp）；
79% 的训练样本存在显著下降变点（BIC 增益>6，均值=24.0），释放位置中位数仅为响应长度的 13%，证明塌陷系统性发生于早期；
随机打乱释放点使 AVG 下降 2.1pp（40.1%→38.0%），证明提升源自轨迹耦合的信号而非简单截断。
2605.13643.ablations_summary: K=4 student top-K 候选集最优（vs K=2/16/32 均低于 40.1%）；使用实现路径 std(A_t) 替代 teacher margin 作释放信号仅得 38.8%，低于 margin 的 40.1%，确认 state-local preference 比 advantage dispersion 更可靠；随机释放对照组验证轨迹特异性必要。
limitations: 实验主要限于 Qwen3 模型族，跨架构泛化性待验证
数学推理领域为主，通用指令遵循等更广场景待探索
当前为离线后处理掩码，不能缩短生成过程；在线截断（rollout-time）留作未来工作
释放规则计算需要对 student top-K 候选集进行 teacher logits 查询，存在额外推理开销
failure_modes: 固定前缀截断（OPD-1024/2048/4096/8192）均不如轨迹自适应截断，表明固定阈值无法捕获样本间的异质性塌陷位置
对较大学生模型（8B）提升收益较小（+0.5pp），暗示强→弱差距越小时局部可教性塌陷效应减弱

theory.theoretical_claim: 通过 Cauchy 不等式证明 OPD 局部期望更新的上界依赖于 teacher 优势在 student 可达集上的动作依赖方差（Var_{a~π_t}(A_t(a))），而非采样 token 优势值；SNR 分析给出后缀释放改善信噪比的充要条件 v_R/v_P ≥ 2(m_R/m_P)+(m_R/m_P)²
theory.proof_sketch: SNR_full=(m_P+m_R)²/(v_P+v_R)，SNR_release=m_P²/v_P；后缀 m_R 小但 v_R 大时，截断后 SNR 提升；BIC 变点检测用 k₀=1 vs k₁=3 参数惩罚自动平衡拟合与复杂度，Δk=2 对应额外的 μ_{post} 和 τ。

2605.13643.relevance_to_opd: 直接针对 OPD 的监督区域问题：诊断了全轨迹密集监督的失效模式（局部可教性塌陷），并提出 BIC 变点检测的轨迹自适应截断方案；属于 OPD 信号质量优化类工作，与 ExOPD、FastOPD 形成对比。

deepseekv4.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
deepseekv4.summary: DeepSeek-V4用纯multi-teacher on-policy distillation替代混合RL阶段进行模型合并，将10+领域专家模型（数学/代码/Agent/指令遵循等）统一蒸馏到单一1.6T MoE模型中，采用full-vocabulary Reverse KL + hidden-state caching + FP4量化感知训练。

method.training_loop: Multi-teacher OPD: student rollout → 逐teacher计算full-vocab KL(通过cached hidden states重建logits) → Reverse KL loss聚合 → 更新student
method.loss_formulation: R-KL: KL(p_student || p_teacher) over full vocabulary at each position, aggregated across 10+ teachers
method.data_source: Student on-policy rollouts, teacher logits reconstructed from cached hidden states
key_components: full-vocabulary KL (not sampled-token)
hidden-state caching with on-the-fly logit reconstruction
teacher-identity-ordered mini-batches
FP4 quantization-aware training during OPD
asynchronous weight loading/offloading

deepseekv4.novelty: 首次在工业规模（1.6T参数）实现纯OPD替代RL进行多专家合并；通过hidden-state caching解决multi-teacher full-vocab KL的内存瓶颈；OPD阶段同步进行FP4量化感知训练消除部署后量化损失。

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: replaces its mixed RL stage with pure multi-teacher OPD for model consolidation; full-vocabulary logit distillation computing the exact KL over all |V| tokens at each position

opd_classification.reasoning: 工业级multi-teacher on-policy distillation应用，student实时生成rollouts，full-vocab KL优化

key_findings: Pure OPD替代混合RL实现模型合并
Full-vocab KL优于sampled-token KL
Hidden-state caching使trillion-scale OPD可行
deepseekv4.ablations_summary: Full-vocabulary vs sampled-token KL对比：full-vocab梯度更稳定，知识迁移更忠实
limitations: 仅限同架构teacher-student（shared vocab）
需要极大GPU集群
未公开具体benchmark数字
deepseekv4.relevance_to_opd: OPD工业化标杆：首次在production中完全替代RL用纯on-policy distillation做multi-expert consolidation。hidden-state caching方案解决了multi-teacher OPD的工程瓶颈。

lu2025onpolicy.title: On-Policy Distillation
lu2025onpolicy.summary: 系统性分析on-policy vs off-policy distillation的区别，重点讨论sampled-token KL（单token策略梯度近似）vs full-vocabulary KL的权衡：前者计算轻量但高方差，后者信息完整但需传输完整logit向量。

method.training_loop: 对比分析：off-policy SFT → on-policy sampled-token KL (policy gradient) → on-policy full-vocab KL distillation
method.loss_formulation: sampled-token: log p_θ(y_t) - log p_T(y_t) as per-token advantage; full-vocab: KL(p_θ(·|y<t) || p_T(·|y<t)) over all |V|
method.data_source: student on-policy rollouts
key_components: sampled-token KL analysis
full-vocabulary KL analysis
gradient variance comparison
bits-per-episode information capacity

lu2025onpolicy.novelty: 首次清晰阐述sampled-token KL = 策略梯度估计（高方差、每episode固定bits数）vs full-vocab KL = 完整分布匹配（低方差、信息密集）的本质区别及工程权衡。

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy training samples rollouts from the student model itself, and assigns them some reward

opd_classification.reasoning: 分析性文章，系统对比sampled-token vs full-vocab KL在OPD中的权衡，被综述§4.1引用讨论full-vocabulary实现

key_findings: RL provides fixed bits per episode regardless of token count
Sampled-token KL = high variance policy gradient estimate
Full-vocab KL preserves distributional information across non-sampled tokens
limitations: 无实验验证
博客格式非peer-reviewed

theory.theoretical_claim: sampled-token KL is a single-sample Monte Carlo estimate of full-vocab KL with O(1) bits per episode
theory.proof_sketch: Information-theoretic argument: binary reward encodes log2(2)=1 bit per episode

lu2025onpolicy.relevance_to_opd: 提供sampled-token vs full-vocab KL的清晰概念框架，被DeepSeek-V4实践验证（full-vocab更优）。综述§4.1引用其对policy gradient估计的分析。

2605.11019.title: Efficient LLM Reasoning via Variational Posterior Guidance with Efficiency Awareness
2605.11019.summary: Variational posterior guidance with efficiency awareness for efficient LLM reasoning

method.teacher: Reference-answer-guided posterior distribution (parameter-shared dual-stream architecture)
method.loss_formulation: Variational distillation (efficiency-aware ELBO objective, KL between posterior and prior policy)

2605.11019.novelty: First application of variational inference theory to LLM reasoning efficiency optimization, with efficiency-aware ELBO, cross-view validation to filter pseudo-efficient paths, and unidirectional variational distillation from posterior to prior within a single shared-parameter model

opd_classification.section: variational inference OPD for efficient reasoning

key_findings: VPG-EA improves ε3 by 8.73% and 12.37% over strongest baselines on 1.5B and 7B respectively
Token consumption reduced by over 30% on MATH-500 (from 2336 to 1626 tokens for 7B)
7B model achieves 93.00% accuracy on MATH-500 with 1626 tokens vs base model 91.00% with 2336 tokens
Removing posterior guidance causes AIME24 accuracy to drop to 16.67% with token surge to 9464
Cross-architecture generalization on Llama-8B shows consistent improvements
2605.11019.ablations_summary: Removing posterior guidance (β=0) severely degrades accuracy and inflates tokens; removing efficiency constraint (α=0) loses length control; α=0.5 is Pareto optimal; excessive α≥1.0 aggressively sacrifices accuracy for marginal token reduction on hard tasks
limitations: Reward hacking remains a fundamental paradigm problem despite cross-view evaluation and advantage gating
Framework strictly depends on deterministic reference answers, limiting applicability to verifiable tasks only
Not applicable to open-domain tasks lacking single standard answers
failure_modes: When α is too large (≥1.0), model aggressively sacrifices accuracy for marginal token reductions on hard tasks
Pseudo-logical shortcuts through topological loopholes in policy space despite filtering

theory.theoretical_claim: Reference-answer-guided posterior distribution has expected utility advantage over prior distribution when Cov_π(L,S)≥0
theory.proof_sketch: Using Bayes theorem and covariance decomposition, E_q[S(z)] - E_π[S(z)] = Cov_π(L,S)/E_π[L] ≥ 0 under non-negative covariance condition

2605.11019.relevance_to_opd: Self-distillation framework where the same model generates on-policy rollouts from both posterior (answer-conditioned) and prior (standard) streams, with variational distillation transferring efficient reasoning patterns from posterior to prior during training
2605.11019.verdict_reason: VPG-EA uses a parameter-shared posterior distribution (conditioned on reference answers) as teacher and performs variational distillation to transfer efficient reasoning patterns to the prior policy. Dual-stream on-policy sampling with cross-view evaluation feeds student rollouts into the distillation loop per iteration.

2605.15239.title: Reducing the Safety Tax in LLM Safety Alignment with On-Policy Self-Distillation
2605.15239.summary: On-policy self-distillation for safety alignment using per-token KL from privileged-context teacher

method.teacher: Frozen copy of base model (pθ₀) conditioned on privileged safety context (Ih/Ib)
method.student: Trainable student model (pθ) — R1-Distill-1.5B, Qwen3-0.6B, etc.
method.loss_formulation: DKL(pT ∥ pS) per token along student rollout

2605.15239.novelty: Adapts on-policy self-distillation to safety alignment via type-conditional privileged contexts and teacher flip rate criterion for context selection, showing off-policy SFT mismatch is a distinct source of safety tax beyond data distribution mismatch
key_findings: OPSA achieves +4.00 composite safety score and +3.04 reasoning avg over ThinkSafe (off-policy SFT) averaged across 5 model configurations
Largest gains on smaller models: +8.85 points on R1-Distill-1.5B and +5.49 points on Qwen3-0.6B
Teacher flip rate (TFR) perfectly predicts post-training effectiveness with Spearman ρ=-1.00 within each model
OPSA drives Prefilling attack ASR to 0% on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B
OPSA wins 24/24 data composition cells on Qwen3-0.6B with +10.3 avg gain, showing robustness to data scarcity
2605.15239.ablations_summary: Divergence ablation (forward vs reverse vs symmetric KL) shows symmetric mix best balances harm reduction and over-refusal; data size sensitivity shows OPSA advantage persists at 10% data; composition grid (6×4) shows OPSA wins 46/48 cells across two models; teacher flip rate validated as monotonic predictor of effectiveness across 3 prompts and 3 models
limitations: Requires base model to retain latent safety capability that privileged context can activate
Teacher is frozen base model; iterative teacher refresh left to future work
Harmfulness measurements depend on Llama-Guard for both filtering and evaluation
Fully adaptive search (PAIR) remains a limitation where OPSA does not consistently improve
failure_modes: PAIR iterative attacker-target-judge search can still break OPSA-aligned models
Models whose safety knowledge has been aggressively overwritten may benefit less due to low teacher flip rate
Mixed results on HumanJailbreaks for R1-Distill family
2605.15239.relevance_to_opd: Directly applies on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) framework to safety alignment domain, demonstrating that on-policy per-token KL supervision from a privileged-context frozen self-teacher reduces safety tax compared to off-policy SFT, providing evidence for OPD's advantage in localized behavioral correction
2605.15239.verdict_reason: OPSA uses a frozen teacher (copy of base model) conditioned on privileged type-conditional safety context, minimizes per-token DKL(pT ∥ pS) along student on-policy rollouts. Student generates rollouts each training step, teacher provides dense KL supervision — textbook on-policy self-distillation.

2605.15532.title: DeltaPrompts: Escaping the Zero-Delta Trap in Multimodal Distillation
2605.15532.summary: Identifies zero-delta prompts in VLM distillation and synthesizes high-divergence prompts for effective on-policy distillation

method.teacher: Stronger VLM teacher (e.g., larger reasoning model providing answer distributions PT)
method.loss_formulation: KL(Pθ(·|x) ∥ PT(·|x)) — distributional divergence minimization

2605.15532.novelty: Identifies that up to 69% of standard dataset prompts are zero-delta (teacher and student agree), proposes answer divergence as a principled prompt selection criterion, and introduces a staged synthesis pipeline that actively targets student failure modes to produce divergence-inducing prompts

on_policy_mechanism.signal_source: Teacher model answer distributions + student trajectory contrast for prompt selection

opd_classification.section: data-centric OPD / prompt selection for multimodal distillation

key_findings: Up to 69% of prompts in standard chart/document reasoning datasets are zero-delta, producing minimal learning signal for distillation.
Delta prompts (Δ>0) scale log-linearly with dataset size while zero-delta prompts saturate immediately regardless of scale.
DeltaPrompts yields up to 15% relative improvement on real-world perception-centric reasoning on top of Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking.
DeltaPrompts transfers to an entirely different model family (GLM) without regenerating data, retaining 154k of 200k prompts.
Augmenting DeltaPrompts with zero-delta prompts degrades performance, confirming zero-delta prompts act as noise.
Skill-guided generation achieves 57% yield of delta prompts vs 31% from filtering existing datasets.
2605.15532.ablations_summary: Zero-delta prompts provide no learning signal even when doubling dataset size; consistency filtering at avg@16≥0.5 is sufficient (stricter thresholds yield no gain); skill-guided generation builds on seed-guided outputs for best yield (57%) and diversity; using off-the-shelf prompts directly for skill-guided generation reduces effectiveness to seed-guided levels.
limitations: Answer divergence is measured once at the start of training and not updated as the student evolves during distillation.
Pipeline generates novel text prompts but still sources images from existing datasets rather than synthesizing them.
Empirical validation focuses on chart, document, and perception-centric reasoning domains only.
failure_modes: Training on HardPrompts (teacher avg@16 < 0.5) degrades performance due to noisy teacher feedback.
Naive filtering for delta prompts from existing datasets reduces diversity by up to 29.4%, limiting effectiveness.
2605.15532.relevance_to_opd: Directly studies on-policy distillation and proposes a data-centric approach (answer divergence-based prompt synthesis) that substantially improves OPD effectiveness by ensuring training prompts expose meaningful teacher-student capability gaps.
2605.15532.verdict_reason: DeltaPrompts evaluates on-policy distillation with an external teacher VLM. The framework uses KL(Pθ(·|x) ∥ PT(·|x)) as the distillation signal, measures answer divergence Δ between student and teacher, and uses student rollouts to identify high-divergence prompts for iterative on-policy distillation training.

2605.18141.title: A Brief Overview: On-Policy Self-Distillation In Large Language Models
2605.18141.summary: Survey/overview of On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) methods for LLMs

method.training_loop: Student generates rollout y~π_stud(·|x); teacher (same model) conditioned on privileged info y* provides token-level supervision; minimize KL/JSD between student and teacher distributions
method.loss_formulation: L_OPSD(θ) = E_{(x,y*)~D, y~π^stud_θ(·|x)} [Σ_t KL(π^stud_θ(·|x,y_{<t}) || π^teach_θ(·|x,y*,y_{<t}))]
method.data_source: problem datasets with ground-truth solutions (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, etc.)
key_components: shared-weight teacher-student with privileged information
on-policy student rollouts
per-token KL/JSD divergence minimization
no external teacher model

2605.18141.novelty: Provides a structured taxonomy and overview of OPSD methods that eliminate external teachers by using privileged information conditioning on the same model, categorizing designs into hybrid policy optimization, feedback-driven distillation, training stability, reasoning compression, capability transfer, and multimodal distillation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: The student generates a rollout y∼π stud(·|x). The teacher then provides token-level supervision for this specific rollout, and the student minimizes the divergence between the two distributions.

opd_classification.reasoning: This is a survey/overview paper analyzing OPSD methods where the same model serves as both teacher and student (pure self-distillation with privileged information), covering multiple design dimensions.

key_findings: OPSD typically reduces GPU memory consumption by approximately 40%-60% compared to standard OPD
OPSD eliminates the need for an external teacher model while providing dense token-level supervision
In extremely large-model scenarios, OPSD is often the only feasible option whereas OPD would lead directly to out-of-memory error
2605.18141.ablations_summary: No empirical ablations presented; this is a survey paper categorizing design principles
limitations: Survey paper without novel empirical contributions
Requires careful handling of privileged information to avoid information leakage
Teacher's rich conditioning can suppress model's expression of uncertainty leading to OOD degradation
failure_modes: Self-distillation signal degeneration or overconfidence from teaching itself
OOD performance degradation when teacher suppresses uncertainty
2605.18141.relevance_to_opd: Directly surveys and taxonomizes On-Policy Self-Distillation methods for LLMs, which is a specialized variant of OPD where the teacher and student share parameters differentiated only by privileged information access

2605.17862.title: f-OPD: Stabilizing Long-Horizon On-Policy Distillation with Freshness-Aware Control
2605.17862.summary: Freshness-aware control framework stabilizing asynchronous on-policy distillation for LLMs

method.teacher: External teacher model providing token-level supervision
method.loss_formulation: OPD distillation loss with freshness-aware sample reweighting and policy drift constraint

2605.17862.novelty: Decomposes asynchronous OPD objective discrepancy into rollout drift and supervision drift, introduces sample-level freshness score quantifying staleness, and proposes three complementary mechanisms to stabilize async OPD without sacrificing throughput
key_findings: f-OPD achieves 39.4 resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified vs 26.8 for vanilla async OPD and 41.8 for sync OPD, with 1.46× throughput gain
Vanilla async OPD with lag=8 degrades coding-agent performance by ~40% compared to synchronous
Freshness weighting alone recovers +9.7 coding resolve and +9.2 tool-use accuracy over vanilla async OPD
f-OPD eliminates training collapse (0/5 runs) while vanilla async OPD collapses in 3/5 runs
2605.17862.ablations_summary: Freshness weighting provides the largest single gain (+9.2/+9.7), rollout-anchored regularization adds +2.4/+1.6, and adaptive refresh eliminates remaining collapse and closes the final gap to synchronous performance
limitations: Experiments cover a small set of model families and tasks
Supervision drift is setting-dependent and may be negligible in static labeling settings
Analysis provides discrepancy bounds under bounded-regularity assumptions, not convergence theory
Calibration coefficients α, β are domain-dependent and not universally optimal
failure_modes: Vanilla async OPD collapses in 3/5 runs on long-horizon coding tasks at lag=8
Hard refresh baseline discards useful learning signals if refreshing too aggressively
Lag-only weighting is insufficient as freshness surrogate when samples with same age have different drift

theory.theoretical_claim: Async OPD objective discrepancy decomposes into rollout drift (TV between current and stale prefix distributions) and supervision drift (TV between current and stale teacher contexts)
theory.proof_sketch: Triangle inequality on intermediate objective pairing stale rollouts with current teacher; Lipschitz loss assumption bounds each term by TV distance; Pinsker's inequality converts to KL diagnostics

2605.17862.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses the systems-level challenge of maintaining on-policy fidelity in asynchronous OPD pipelines, proposes freshness-aware mechanisms to stabilize long-horizon on-policy distillation at scale
2605.17862.verdict_reason: f-OPD is explicitly an on-policy distillation framework with external teacher supervision, student rollouts per training step, and distillation loss. It addresses staleness in asynchronous OPD via freshness scoring. Standard OPD pipeline: student rollout → teacher supervision → distillation optimization.

2605.18740.title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation
2605.18740.affiliation_primary: Chinese Information Processing Laboratory, Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences
2605.18740.summary: Regional-to-global on-policy self-distillation for fine-grained visual understanding in MLLMs

method.teacher: Same MLLM conditioned on evidence-centered crops (privileged regional perception)
method.student: Same MLLM conditioned on full images
method.loss_formulation: Token-level KL divergence between crop-conditioned teacher and full-image student next-token distributions

2605.18740.novelty: First to use the same MLLM's crop-conditioned behavior as privileged teacher for its full-image policy via on-policy distillation, without external teachers, ground-truth labels, or reward verifiers, specifically targeting the regional-to-global perception gap in fine-grained visual understanding.
key_findings: Vision-OPD-9B achieves 75.70 average across 6 fine-grained benchmarks, surpassing Gemini-3.1-Pro (74.74) and Qwen3.5-397B (72.54).
Vision-OPD-4B achieves 73.83 average, outperforming GPT-5.4 (68.42) with only 4B parameters.
Vision-OPD maintains or improves holdout task performance while SFT and RLVR baselines degrade.
On-policy self-distillation substantially narrows the regional-to-global perception gap during training.
Only 6.2K synthetic training samples are needed for significant improvements.
2605.18740.ablations_summary: EMA teacher regularization is critical (current policy without regularization collapses to 0%); JSD(β=0.5) outperforms forward KL and reverse KL; longer rollouts (1024 vs 512 tokens) improve performance; top-K logits distillation outperforms sampled-token objectives.
2605.18740.relevance_to_opd: Directly instantiates on-policy distillation for multimodal LLMs where a self-teacher (crop-conditioned) provides dense token-level supervision on student (full-image) rollouts, demonstrating OPD's effectiveness in visual reasoning without external teachers or rewards.
2605.18740.verdict_reason: Crop-conditioned teacher and full-image-conditioned student from same MLLM; student generates on-policy rollouts and training minimizes token-level divergence between teacher and student next-token distributions along those rollouts.

2605.16826.title: Decoupling KL and Trajectories: A Unified Perspective for SFT, DAgger, Offline RL, and OPD in LLM Distillation
2605.16826.summary: Decouples prefix source and KL direction in LLM distillation yielding four objectives with tradeoff analysis

method.training_loop: Decouple prefix source (teacher/student) × KL direction (forward/reverse) into 4 token-level distillation objectives; propose KL mixing and entropy-gated length curriculum
method.data_source: DeepScaleR math reasoning dataset
key_components: decoupled prefix-source × KL-direction framework
KL mixing
entropy-gated length curriculum
fused full-vocabulary KL kernel

2605.16826.novelty: Identifies and systematically studies the implicit coupling of prefix source and KL direction in sequence-level KL distillation, revealing two novel off-diagonal objectives (teacher-prefix reverse KL as offline RL, student-prefix forward KL as DAgger), and proposes KL mixing and entropy-gated curriculum to balance accuracy-entropy tradeoffs

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) instead lets the student generate its own rollouts at training time and uses the teacher's per-token log-probabilities as a dense supervision signal on the states the student visits

opd_classification.reasoning: The paper's core contribution is a theoretical framework unifying four distillation objectives and empirical analysis of their tradeoffs, rather than proposing a single new OPD method.

key_findings: Reverse KL improves Avg@k by +2.45 points on average over forward KL but causes entropy collapse and length inflation
Student prefixes improve Avg@k by +1.80 and Pass@k by +2.11 points on average over teacher prefixes
Entropy-gated length curriculum improves Avg@k by 3.6 points and Pass@k by up to 5.8 points while reducing response length by ~3× vs fixed 4096-token training
Forward KL preserves entropy and supports more stable downstream RL improvement despite weaker standalone performance
Long-sequence distillation requires substantial forward-KL weight to prevent entropy collapse and length inflation
2605.16826.ablations_summary: Systematic 2×2 ablation of prefix source (teacher/student) × KL direction (forward/reverse) across two training lengths (128/4096 tokens), two teacher scales (4B/8B), both standalone and as RL initialization; KL mixing weight sweep; entropy-gated curriculum vs fixed-length
limitations: Study focuses only on mathematical reasoning domain
RL follow-up uses only GRPO with accuracy-only reward
Does not explore other RL algorithms or domains like code generation
failure_modes: Reverse KL with long-sequence training drives entropy to collapse and causes severe length inflation
Reverse-KL warm starts can degrade during subsequent RL due to low entropy constraining exploration
4096-token reverse-KL distillation pushes response lengths to generation limit

theory.theoretical_claim: Forward KL gradient equals cross-entropy with teacher soft targets; reverse KL gradient equals REINFORCE with dense log-ratio reward; sequence-level KL decomposes into token-level KL under respective prefix distributions
theory.proof_sketch: Proposition 1 proves (i) ∇_θ KL(p_T||q_θ) = -E_{y~p_T}[∇_θ log q_θ(y|s_t)] and (ii) ∇_θ KL(q_θ||p_T) = E_{y~q_θ}[(log q_θ - log p_T) ∇_θ log q_θ] via score-function identity

2605.16826.relevance_to_opd: Directly analyzes on-policy distillation as one of four decoupled objectives (student-prefix reverse KL), characterizes its tradeoffs vs off-policy alternatives, and proposes stabilization methods (KL mixing, entropy-gated curriculum) for OPD

2605.17497.title: Self-Supervised On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning Language Models
2605.17497.summary: Self-supervised on-policy distillation from intra-group correct-wrong contrast in GRPO

method.teacher: Stop-gradient copy of model conditioned on successful completion (self-generated witness)
method.student: Same model (Qwen3-8B, etc.) trained with GRPO + auxiliary distillation loss
method.loss_formulation: Token-level KL distillation from teacher (conditioned on correct witness) to student at failed prefixes, weighted by prompt-level frontier weight

2605.17497.novelty: Converts intra-group correct-wrong contrast from GRPO rollouts into dense process supervision via self-distillation without external solution traces, using a stopping-time-motivated shortest-correct/longest-wrong selection rule and frontier weighting

on_policy_mechanism.signal_source: Self-generated correct completions as privileged hindsight (no external teacher)

opd_classification.section: self-supervised on-policy distillation for math reasoning

key_findings: SSOPD improves over GRPO in all nine model-benchmark settings without additional solution traces
On Qwen3-8B, SSOPD reaches macro Avg@12 of 65.6, outperforming GRPO by 1.6 points and OPSD by 0.8 points
Dynamic frontier weight improves over fixed weighting at every tested value of λ_0
Shortest-correct/longest-wrong selector pair achieves best performance (45.0 Avg@12) among all selector combinations
2605.17497.ablations_summary: Dynamic frontier weight (λ_0=0.5 best among 0.4-0.7) outperforms fixed global coefficient; shortest-correct/longest-wrong pairing is best among 12 selector combinations on HMMT2025
limitations: Relies on reliable answer verification and useful correct witnesses from the current policy
May be weaker outside mathematical reasoning or for smaller models
At smaller scales (1.7B, 4B) OPSD with external solutions remains stronger
failure_modes: When model rarely solves a prompt, no reliable successful witness exists
When model always solves a prompt, few representative failures exist

theory.theoretical_claim: Local improvement by reweighting good futures (Theorem 3.1) and stopping-time-aware SSOPD lower bound (Theorem 3.2)
theory.proof_sketch: Theorem 3.1 shows local edit toward desirability-posterior improves value by Var[Q]/V; Theorem 3.2 extends to teacher-approximated edits with bounded error; Proposition 3.3 shows frontier coefficient equals branching variance via martingale decomposition

2605.17497.relevance_to_opd: Proposes a pure on-policy self-distillation method where the student's own successful rollouts serve as teacher context at failed prefixes, directly advancing OPD by eliminating external teacher/trace dependence
2605.17497.verdict_reason: SSOPD distills a stop-gradient teacher (conditioned on the shortest correct self-generated completion) into the student at prefixes of the longest wrong completion. Uses on-policy GRPO group rollouts per training step; the teacher distribution is constructed from the same policy's successful samples as privileged hindsight.

2605.17873.title: HINT-SD: Targeted Hindsight Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
2605.17873.summary: Targeted self-distillation selecting failure-relevant turns for long-horizon agent training

method.teacher: Same model conditioned on full-trajectory hindsight feedback (textual critiques/hints)
method.loss_formulation: Token-level distillation loss on targeted action spans (teacher conditioned on hindsight → student)

2605.17873.novelty: Unlike prior methods that apply feedback uniformly across trajectories or at every turn, HINT-SD uses full-trajectory hindsight to select failure-relevant turns and applies feedback-conditioned self-distillation only at those targeted action spans, improving both effectiveness and efficiency.

on_policy_mechanism.signal_source: Full-trajectory hindsight feedback (textual critiques from failed trajectories)

opd_classification.section: targeted on-policy self-distillation for long-horizon agents

key_findings: HINT-SD-Multi improves BFCL v3 Avg@4 from 31.56 (best baseline) to 41.88 (+10.32 pp) and AppWorld Avg@4 from 9.74 to 18.46 (+8.72 pp)
HINT-SD achieves 2.26× lower time per training step and 1.48× lower peak GPU memory than the dense-feedback baseline
Target-turn feedback yields +5.99 pp gain over start-of-trajectory feedback on BFCL v3
Even HINT-SD-Single (distilling only first failure-relevant step) substantially outperforms all baselines on both benchmarks
Later target turns (9+) increase from 14.0% to 24.5% over training, suggesting feedback shifts to later-stage corrections as early errors are resolved
2605.17873.ablations_summary: Key ablations: (1) Single vs Multi target selection shows multi-step distillation extracts richer corrective signal; (2) Feedback placement at target turn vs start yields +5.99 pp on BFCL; (3) Feedback source comparison shows EMA teacher > fixed initial teacher > environment feedback, and larger external teacher (GPT-5.4-mini) provides further gains.
limitations: Training signal depends on whether generated feedback correctly identifies actionable failures and proposes useful corrections
Requires the initial model to have sufficient instruction-following and task-solving capability to reason about failed trajectories
failure_modes: When the model cannot generate accurate hindsight feedback due to insufficient reasoning capability
When feedback misidentifies root causes in very long trajectories
2605.17873.relevance_to_opd: HINT-SD is an on-policy self-distillation method where the student generates rollouts during training, selects failure-relevant turns via hindsight analysis, and distills from its own feedback-conditioned distribution (teacher) into the feedback-free policy (student) using reverse KL on selected action spans.
2605.17873.verdict_reason: HINT-SD uses feedback-conditioned self-distillation where a teacher (same model conditioned on full-trajectory hindsight feedback) provides token-level supervision on targeted failure-relevant action spans. Student generates on-policy rollouts, hindsight identifies failure spans, teacher distills corrective behavior.

2605.18299.title: SD-Search: On-Policy Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Reasoning
2605.18299.summary: On-policy hindsight self-distillation for step-level search query supervision in RL

method.teacher: Same model conditioned on compact hindsight block (search queries + outcomes of group rollouts)
method.student: Same model without hindsight (inference-time conditioning only)
method.loss_formulation: Token-level Jensen-Shannon divergence DJS(teacher ∥ student) at search-query positions

2605.18299.novelty: Derives step-level supervision for search queries from the policy itself via hindsight conditioning on sibling rollout outcomes, replacing external teacher models or auxiliary annotations required by prior process-supervision methods

on_policy_mechanism.signal_source: Self-generated hindsight from group rollout outcomes (no external model)

key_findings: SD-Search-Base (3B) reaches 0.428 avg EM, matching Thinker-Instruct (0.430) which uses a 72B external teacher, without any external model.
SD-Search-Instruct (7B) reaches 0.476 avg EM, surpassing AutoRefine by +2.1 and Thinker by +2.4 points.
Gains are concentrated on multi-hop benchmarks: Bamboogle +5.8, MuSiQue +3.1, 2Wiki +2.7 over AutoRefine-Base at 3B.
SD-Search adds only 15.5% end-to-end training wall-clock overhead with no inference cost increase.
SD-Search's gain comes from higher query quality at comparable search frequency, not from issuing more searches.
2605.18299.ablations_summary: Removing outcome labels costs 1.4 points; shuffling labels costs 2.3; removing future masking costs 3.0; replacing full hindsight with current-step docs costs 3.4; JSD outperforms forward KL by 1.0, reverse KL by 1.4, MSE by 2.1; broadening scope from Q_τ to A_τ costs 0.7 points.
limitations: Relies on gold answers for outcome labels, restricting to tasks with reliably scorable references
Hindsight contrast degenerates when rollout group becomes label-homogeneous (all-success or all-failure)
failure_modes: At 14B scale, high base success rates make group-uniform CORRECT labels more frequent, narrowing SD-Search's gain
All-failure groups cause both GRPO advantages and hindsight contrast to collapse simultaneously
2605.18299.relevance_to_opd: Proposes on-policy self-distillation where the same policy generates rollouts and serves as its own teacher via hindsight conditioning, producing dense token-level supervision signals within the RL training loop without any external teacher model.
2605.18299.verdict_reason: SD-Search uses a self-teacher conditioned on a hindsight block (summarizing rollout outcomes) and minimizes token-level Jensen-Shannon divergence to the student at search-query positions. Fully on-policy: signal produced by the policy itself within the standard GRPO training loop per step.

2605.16865.title: MIXSD: Mixed Contextual Self-Distillation for Knowledge Injection
2605.16865.summary: Self-distillation via Bernoulli mixing of expert and naive base-model conditionals for knowledge injection without forgetting

method.training_loop: For each example, generate mixed supervision by sampling expert (fact-in-context) or naive (no-fact) token from base model at each step with Bernoulli(λ), then train student with NLL on mixed targets
method.loss_formulation: L_MIXSD(θ;λ) = -E_{(x,y*)~D} E_{y+,y-} Σ_t log p_θ(y^mix_{i,t} | x_i, y^mix_{i,<t})
method.data_source: Synthetic KGFACT/KGFUNC datasets, SimpleQA, MQuAKE
key_components: expert conditional (fact-in-context rollout from base model)
naive conditional (no-fact rollout from base model)
per-token Bernoulli mixing with rate λ
NLL training on mixed targets

2605.16865.novelty: Constructs distribution-aligned supervision by per-token Bernoulli mixing between expert-conditioned (fact in context) and naive-conditioned rollouts from the same base model, requiring no external teacher and reducing Fisher-sensitive parameter displacement

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: generating mixed rollouts incurs a one-time preprocessing cost over standard SFT, though this is substantially smaller than the per-step cost of on-policy self-distillation

opd_classification.reasoning: MIXSD generates mixed supervision targets offline (one-time preprocessing) from the base model before training, not during the training loop; it is off-policy self-distillation for knowledge injection, not on-policy distillation.

stabilization_tricks: rule-based verifier with up to 10 retries for correct rollouts

key_findings: MIXSD (λ=0.5) retains up to 100% of base model capability while maintaining near-perfect training accuracy, vs SFT retaining as little as 1%
Fisher alignment ratio R correlates strongly with forgetting (r=+0.82 for 4B model) while raw displacement shows weak correlation (r=+0.02)
MIXSD reduces high-NLL tokens (NLL>8) from 27-42% (SFT) to 4-8% (λ=0.3) of supervision targets
On Qwen3-4B-It KGFACT-SMALL, MIXSD (λ=0.5) achieves 89% training accuracy and 77.5% avg held-out vs SFT's 100%/43.2%
SFT errors are dominated by leakage (50.7%) and collapse (48.0%) on MMLU, while MIXSD errors are ≥71% genuine reasoning errors
2605.16865.ablations_summary: λ controls injection-retention trade-off (0→0.7); KL-based objectives underfit target knowledge (34-60% accuracy) vs NLL (96-100%); OPSD requires 8 rollouts but is inconsistent across scales; effect transfers to Llama family; method works for knowledge editing (MQuAKE)
limitations: Hyperparameter λ may need tuning for other tasks
Largest model tested is 8B; scaling to 70B+ is unverified
Generating mixed rollouts incurs a one-time preprocessing cost over standard SFT
failure_modes: At small model scale (1.7B), MIXSD still shows notable forgetting compared to larger models
MIXSD (λ=0) without naive mixing shows limited forgetting reduction, similar to SFT at small scale
High λ (0.7) noticeably degrades memorization of injected knowledge

theory.theoretical_claim: Forgetting is driven by per-token mismatch between supervision targets and reference model distribution; Fisher-weighted displacement along sensitive directions predicts forgetting better than raw magnitude
theory.proof_sketch: Fisher alignment ratio R = (∆θ^T F̂ ∆θ / ||∆θ||²) / (tr(F̂)/d) correlates with forgetting (r up to +0.82), while raw displacement does not (r as low as +0.02)

2605.16865.relevance_to_opd: Proposes an offline self-distillation method that explicitly contrasts with on-policy self-distillation (OPSD baseline); constructs distribution-aligned targets from the model itself without on-policy training loop, serving as a simpler alternative to on-policy KD for knowledge injection

2605.19433.title: Backtracking When It Strays: Mitigating Dual Exposure Biases in LLM Reasoning Distillation
2605.19433.summary: MOTAB monitors student on-policy trajectories and backtracks to safe states for teacher correction to resolve dual exposure biases in reasoning distillation

method.teacher: Larger teacher model (e.g., DeepSeek-level) providing token probabilities as dense feedback
method.student: Compact student model (trained on LIMO-v2 and AceReason datasets)
method.loss_formulation: Token-level KL guided by teacher token probabilities along student on-policy trajectories with backtracking to teacher intervention at safety boundary violations

2605.19433.novelty: Identifies reversed exposure bias in on-policy distillation (teacher fails on student sub-optimal contexts) and resolves dual biases via adaptive monitoring with backtracking to safe states for teacher intervention, unlike SKD which immediately corrects deviations
key_findings: MOTAB achieves average accuracy of 66.64% with Qwen3-32B teacher, over 7% improvement vs strongest SKD baseline on Qwen3-4B student
With gpt-oss-120b teacher, MOTAB reaches 77.62% average, 2.5% above best SKD variant
Disabling state backtracking causes most severe ablation decline (34.17% to 30.83% on AIME24 P@1)
MOTAB generalizes to cross-domain tasks: IFEval and GPQA show consistent improvements
On-policy comparison with Qwen3-8B→Qwen3-1.7B shows MOTAB comparable to top-k OPD while being more compute efficient
2605.19433.ablations_summary: Removing adaptive boundary (w/o adapt) drops AIME24 P@1 from 34.17 to 32.50; removing backtracking (w/o back) causes largest drop to 30.83; removing stitching (w/o stitch) drops to 32.08. All components contribute, with backtracking being most critical.
limitations: Additional computational overhead during data synthesis phase due to continuous monitoring and teacher-student interactions
Sensitivity to threshold γ0 parameter requiring moderate tuning
failure_modes: Overly low γ0 is too lenient, failing to catch severe logical drifts and permitting error cascades
Excessively high γ0 becomes overly rigid, constantly interrupting natural exploration and discarding acceptable sub-optimal paths

theory.theoretical_claim: Off-policy distillation error compounds at O(L²ε); on-policy distillation causes teacher entropy collapse to uniform; MOTAB satisfies both coverage and validity conditions of the ideal unbiased objective
theory.proof_sketch: Theorem 1 shows off-policy sequence-level divergence grows O(L²) via telescoping TV distance; Theorem 2 shows teacher conditional distribution degenerates to uniform on sub-optimal student contexts; Theorems 4-5 prove MOTAB's truncated distribution covers student's authentic manifold while teacher operates on pristine safe states

2605.19433.relevance_to_opd: Directly addresses the core challenge of on-policy distillation by identifying reversed exposure bias and proposing a monitoring-backtracking mechanism that maintains valid teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories
2605.19433.verdict_reason: MOTAB is explicitly an on-policy distillation method where student generates own reasoning trajectories guided by teacher's dense token-level feedback (token probabilities), with a dynamic monitoring/backtracking mechanism to handle dual exposure bias.

2605.13724.title: AnyFlow: Any-Step Video Diffusion Model with On-Policy Flow Map Distillation
2605.13724.summary: AnyFlow 提出两阶段视频扩散蒸馏框架：先用 MeanFlow 目标学习任意 (t,r) 时间对的 flow map，再用 Flow Map Backward Simulation (FMBS) 将 Euler rollout 分解为 shortcut 段进行在线策略 DMD 蒸馏，解决一致性蒸馏随步数增加质量下降的问题，Wan2.1-14B 在 VBench 上达到 84.41。

method.training_loop: Stage1: 在 256K 合成视频上用 MeanFlow 目标微调 Wan2.1，学习任意时间对 flow map，2 forward passes/step 估计 du/dt。Stage2: 从 Stage1 ckpt 出发，每步先用 FMBS 分解 T-step rollout（shortcut→target-step→shortcut），再对生成帧重新加噪，frozen teacher 提供 s_real，student discriminator 提供 s_fake，反向 DMD gradient 经 FMBS 链 backprop；训练时随机采样 step budget N，800 iter。
method.loss_formulation:
Stage1: L(θ) = E[‖u_θ(z_t, r, t) − sg(u_tgt)‖²], u_tgt = v(z_t,t) − (t−r)·(du_θ/dt)
Stage2 (DMD): ∇_θ L_DMD = −E[(s_real(z_t,t) − s_fake(z_t,t)) · ∂f_θ(z)/∂θ]
method.data_source: 256K 合成 prompt-video 对，由 Wan2.1-T2V-14B 生成（81帧, 480×832）
key_components: Two-time flow map formulation (任意 (t,r) 对)
Flow Map Backward Simulation (FMBS) 在线策略蒸馏
MeanFlow 目标 + finite-difference du/dt 估计
CFG baked-in 训练 (guidance-fused)
Beta(2,1.5) 时间采样
LoRA rank=256 参数高效微调

2605.13724.novelty: 现有一致性蒸馏（rCM）用一致性采样轨迹替代 PF-ODE，中间状态重加噪导致多步退化；AnyFlow 的 FMBS 将完整 rollout 分解为无梯度 shortcut + 有梯度 target-step + 无梯度 shortcut，不重加噪，避免轨迹漂移，使同一模型可在 2-32 步自由伸缩且质量单调提升。

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: In Stage 2, for each training iteration, we sample noise z_T, then run FMBS: z_T → z_t via shortcut (no grad), z_t → z_r via the target step (with grad), z_r → ẑ₀ via shortcut (with grad). We then re-noise ẑ₀ to compute the DMD gradient using frozen teacher score s_real and student discriminator s_fake, backpropagating through the full FMBS chain. By varying N during training, the model learns all step counts with the same computational cost.

opd_classification.reasoning: 核心贡献是视频扩散这一新兴领域的在线策略蒸馏系统（AnyFlow），使用 FMBS 实现每步 student rollout + DMD 目标，属于新领域 OPD 应用。
opd_classification.rejected_reason: Video generation (Wan2.1-14B + VBench). Per 5/15 scope: video output not collected.

key_findings: AnyFlow-FAR-Wan2.1-14B 在 32 NFEs 下达到 VBench 84.41，超越 Krea-Realtime-14B（83.25），且 4 NFEs 仍达 84.05，同一模型实现任意步数自适应推理。
rCM（一致性蒸馏基线）从 2→32 NFEs VBench 由 82.81 下降至 75.72（−7.09），而 AnyFlow 从 82.92 提升至 83.96（+1.04），彻底解决多步退化问题。
FMBS 在 4 步时计算成本仅比 consistency BS 高 15.7%，而在 16 步时比 consistency BS 低 43.4%，当 shortcut 段占主导时效率更优。
2605.13724.ablations_summary: 消融显示：(1) Flow map training > consistency ODE-Init（多步伸缩能力更强）；(2) FMBS 是关键，去除后 32-NFE VBench 从 83.96 降至 82.96；(3) Beta(2,1.5) 时间采样优于 Uniform/Normal；(4) Interpolated timestep conditioning 防止过饱和。
limitations: 依赖外部合成数据集进行 flow map 训练，合成数据分布与 base model 存在轻微分布偏移，导致纹理略微平滑。
下游特定域（机器人、自动驾驶）仍需额外微调。
failure_modes: 一致性蒸馏（rCM baseline）在多步（>4 NFEs）时质量单调下降（82.81→75.72 at 32 NFEs），AnyFlow 通过 FMBS 避免此问题。

theory.theoretical_claim: Flow map composition property: f_θ(z_t,t,q) ≈ f_θ(f_θ(z_t,t,r),r,q)，FMBS shortcut 分解的理论基础
theory.proof_sketch: 基于 PF-ODE 的 flow map identity 和 composition 性质（Eq. 8），证明 FMBS 将 T-step rollout 分解为 shortcut 段时保持轨迹一致性；无严格收敛证明，为描述性/动机性理论。

2605.13724.relevance_to_opd: AnyFlow 是视频扩散领域的在线策略蒸馏应用：Stage 2 每训练步实时采样 student rollout（via FMBS），用 frozen teacher 评分提供 DMD 梯度信号，属于标准 on-policy KD 范式；FMBS 是核心创新，确保反向传播能穿越完整多步轨迹而不引入重加噪漂移。
2605.13724.rejected_reason: Video generation (Wan2.1-14B + VBench). Per 5/15 scope: video output not collected.

2605.20643.title: AVSD: Adaptive-View Self-Distillation by Balancing Consensus and Teacher-Specific Privileged Signals
2605.20643.summary: Multi-view on-policy self-distillation separating consensus from view-specific residual signals

method.teacher: Same model in teacher mode conditioned on privileged information (3 views: full solution, partial CoT rationale, gold answer)
method.student: Same model in student mode (no privileged information)
method.loss_formulation: Token-level KL with geometric target combining consensus across views plus gated view-specific residuals

2605.20643.novelty: Decomposes multi-view privileged teacher signals into geometric consensus and gated residual, preventing any single privileged view from dominating the token-level update while preserving complementary information

opd_classification.section: on-policy self-distillation with multi-view privileged information

key_findings: AVSD improves Avg@8 by 3.1% over strongest baseline on Qwen3-8B across math benchmarks
AVSD improves Avg@8 by 2.2% over strongest baseline on Qwen3-4B across math benchmarks
On code benchmarks (Qwen3-8B), AVSD outperforms single-view OPSD by 2.4% on average
OPSD assigns incorrect-sign credit to 12.3% of high-impact tokens vs only 2.9% for AVSD
Gate-open rate is consistently 21-27% across models, showing selective residual usage
AVSD adds only 1.13× runtime overhead over single-view OPSD
2605.20643.ablations_summary: Consensus-only and arithmetic-only variants both underperform full AVSD by 1.4% and 1.7% on average respectively; scaling from 1 to 3 views improves AIME24 by 2.9%; 4th view shows diminishing returns on math but continued gains on code
limitations: Validated primarily on math and code reasoning tasks; broader settings like tool-use agents not tested
Depends on quality of constructed views and underlying data quality
Instantiated with reverse-KL only; guarantees may not transfer to other divergences
failure_modes: Noisy annotated solutions may lead to less reliable teacher signals
Fourth view shows diminishing returns when main privilege sources are already covered

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: M× prefill-only forward passes (no additional rollouts)

theory.theoretical_claim: Bounded residual property: gated residual cannot flip consensus direction (λ_t(v)J_t(v) ≤ |A^G_t(v)|)
theory.proof_sketch: Since C_t(v) ∈ [0,1] and J_t(v)/(|A^G_t(v)|+J_t(v)+ε) ≤ 1, the product λ_t(v)J_t(v) ≤ |A^G_t(v)|, preserving consensus sign

2605.20643.relevance_to_opd: Directly advances on-policy self-distillation by introducing multi-view privileged information aggregation with gated consensus-residual decomposition for token-level learning signals
2605.20643.verdict_reason: Self-distillation with multiple privileged-information views (full solution, partial CoT, answer-only) as teachers; student generates on-policy rollouts, teacher modes provide token-level KL targets via geometric consensus with gated residual signals.

2605.22240.title: Unlocking Proactivity in Task-Oriented Dialogue
2605.22240.summary: Asymmetric on-policy self-distillation from privileged user concerns for proactive TOD

method.teacher: Same policy conditioned on privileged view (user's latent concerns visible)
method.student: Same policy in deployable mode (conversation-only view, no access to latent concerns)
method.loss_formulation: KL-based self-distillation from privileged-view teacher to conversation-only student (asymmetric on-policy self-distillation)

2605.22240.novelty: Introduces asymmetric self-distillation where the same policy under a privileged view (conditioned on latent user concerns) serves as teacher for its deployable view, combined with simulator state-transition credit assignment, eliminating the need for separate teacher models or external reward models

opd_classification.section: on-policy self-distillation / task-oriented dialogue with privileged information

key_findings: SI-AVPO on Qwen3-4B achieves 51.9% CSR and 46.3% Acc on Merchant scene, surpassing Claude-Sonnet-4.5 on CSR (51.1%)
SI-AVPO on Qwen3-8B surpasses best RL baseline (SEAD) by +12.2% CSR, +12.2% Acc, and +0.55 Proactivity on merchant scene
Removing AOPD causes CSR to drop by 16.5% and Acc by 11.8%, confirming asymmetric distillation is essential
OPD with stronger Qwen3-32B teacher but no privileged info yields 7.0% lower CSR than AOPD, confirming information asymmetry is key
SI-AVPO generalizes across 6 unseen user simulators with average +14.8% CSR and +15.5% Acc improvements on Qwen3-4B
2605.22240.ablations_summary: AOPD removal causes -16.5% CSR/-11.8% Acc with largest proactivity decline (-0.76); STPR removal causes -7.3% CSR/-7.6% Acc but proactivity increases (overly aggressive); turn-level reward removal causes -5.2% CSR/-4.1% Acc; replacing AOPD with vanilla OPD (Qwen3-32B teacher, no P^int) yields -14.3% CSR/-13.5% Acc vs full model
2605.22240.relevance_to_opd: Proposes Asymmetric On-Policy Self-Distillation (AOPD) where a single policy's privileged view (conditioned on hidden user concerns) distills into its deployable view using on-policy rollouts, a novel form of on-policy self-distillation for multi-turn dialogue
2605.22240.verdict_reason: Uses Asymmetric On-Policy Self-Distillation that transfers concern-aware behavior from a privileged view (same policy conditioned on user's latent concerns) into the deployable conversation-only view, with on-policy rollouts generated through simulator interactions.

2605.21924.title: Visual-Advantage On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
2605.21924.summary: Token-level visual advantage reweighting for on-policy VLM distillation

method.teacher: Larger Qwen3-VL models (4B, 8B, 32B) scoring student rollouts
method.loss_formulation: Token-level KL with VA-based reweighting: rollout-level by trajectory-averaged VA, token-level KL averaged separately within high-VA and low-VA groups

2605.21924.novelty: Introduces visual advantage (teacher log-prob difference with/without fine-grained visual detail) as token-level signal and uses it at two granularities (rollout-level reweighting and token-level grouped KL) to prevent dilution of visual supervision in VLM on-policy distillation

opd_classification.section: on-policy distillation / vision-language with visual-advantage weighting

key_findings: VA-OPD improves over Standard OPD on all 8 benchmarks with Math Avg +2.9 and Visual Avg +1.5 in the primary 8B→2B setting
Gains grow monotonically with teacher size: +2.1/+0.8 (4B), +2.9/+1.5 (8B), +3.7/+2.0 (32B) for Math/Visual Avg
Scaling from Geometry3K to ViRL39K amplifies gains from +2.9 to +3.8 on Math Avg and +1.5 to +2.5 on Visual Avg
VA-OPD achieves ~3.0× wall-clock speedup to reach Standard OPD's final accuracy on MathVerse
Top 10% of tokens by VA carry ~93% of total VA mass, and masking them drops accuracy by ~2.9 points
2605.21924.ablations_summary: Both rollout-level reweighting and token-level grouped KL contribute independently; removing either degrades performance. Full VA-OPD achieves +2.8 on MathVerse, +2.5 on HallusionBench, +1.7 on OCRBench over Standard OPD.
limitations: VA measures teacher-relative counterfactual sensitivity, not direct internal perceptual processes
Strongest gains on vision-intensive tasks; improvements on benchmarks solvable from text alone (e.g., MMStar) are more modest
failure_modes: Benchmarks where questions are solvable from text alone show only modest improvements

compute_efficiency.teacher_inference_cost: 1× + one extra forward pass with degraded image

2605.21924.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation (GKD/MiniLLM) to vision-language models by introducing visual advantage as a token-level reweighting signal that addresses the unique challenge of sparse visual supervision in VLM rollouts
2605.21924.verdict_reason: VA-OPD is explicitly on-policy distillation for VLMs: student generates rollouts, teacher (larger Qwen3-VL model) scores them with token-level KL, reweighted by visual advantage (log-prob difference with/without fine-grained visual detail) at both rollout and token level.

2605.21851.title: OPPO: Bayesian Value Recursion for Token-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Reasoning
2605.21851.summary: Bayesian value recursion for token-level credit in RLVR via oracle-conditioned likelihood ratios

method.teacher: Self-oracle (student conditioned on ground-truth answer) or teacher-oracle (stronger frozen model conditioned on answer)
method.loss_formulation: Policy gradient with token-level advantage from Bayesian value recursion: advantage = log λ_t * state_weight (not standalone KL, but oracle-derived advantage modulation)

2605.21851.novelty: Identifies that the OPD per-token log-ratio is a Bayesian sufficient statistic for success probability, accumulates it into a closed-form running value estimate V_t, and modulates credit by V_t(1-V_t) state weight to concentrate gradients on pivotal tokens without a learned critic
key_findings: Teacher-OPPO on DAPO achieves +5.7 on AMC'23 and +5.2 on AIME'24 over DAPO baseline on Qwen3-4B
Self-OPPO (no external teacher) outperforms GRPO by up to +4.5 on AMC'23 and +3.1 on AIME'24
Gains widen monotonically with response length: Self-OPPO achieves 62.8% vs GRPO's 52.0% on 1025+ token responses
Oracle quality scales monotonically with teacher size, with largest jump at 4B-to-8B transition
Direction anchoring is the most critical component; removing it drops AIME'24 below GRPO
2605.21851.ablations_summary: Direction anchoring is most important (removal drops AIME'24 from 49.5 to 43.0, below GRPO's 46.4). State tracking V_t(1-V_t) ranks second (removal: 46.8). Evidence clipping contributes modestly (48.6 without). Using logλ_t only without state tracking or clipping approaches GRPO performance (46.5 vs 46.4).
limitations: Requires verifiable ground-truth answers for oracle conditioning; extending beyond domains with verifiable answers remains open
Teacher-oracle adds ~95% wall-clock overhead due to separate 32B model scoring
Uncorrelated score-vector assumption in variance reduction proof does not hold for autoregressive models
Evidence clipping prevents exact telescoping; residual grows with sequence length
failure_modes: Without direction anchoring, tokens with logλ_t>0 in incorrect trajectories receive positive advantage, reinforcing flawed reasoning
On very long sequences, evidence clipping caps the recursion and the telescoping residual grows

theory.theoretical_claim: Bayesian value recursion telescopes to R-V_0 and V_t(1-V_t) modulation provides directional variance reduction over state-blind weighting
theory.proof_sketch: Under uncorrelated score vectors, Var[g_blind]-Var[g_Bayes] ≥ (1-γ²)Σ_{t∈D}(logλ_t)²Var[h_t] where D={t: |logλ_t|≥δ, V_t(1-V_t)<γ}

2605.21851.relevance_to_opd: Directly extends on-policy distillation by showing that the OPD per-token log-ratio logλ_t is simultaneously the Bayesian sufficient statistic for V_t; recovers pure OPD as a strict special case (self-oracle without state tracking or direction anchoring); demonstrates that accumulating the OPD signal via Bayesian recursion yields superior token-level credit assignment
2605.21851.verdict_reason: OPPO explicitly derives OPD as strict special case (Eq 5-6). Core signal is teacher log-ratio log λ = log π_T - log π_θ (= KL gradient). Extends with Bayesian V_t(1-V_t) credit assignment. Teacher-oracle + standalone KL connection = Path A.

2605.22478.title: Matching with Deliberation: Test-Time Evolutionary Hierarchical Multi-Agents for Zero-Shot Compositional Image Retrieval
2605.22478.summary: Hierarchical multi-agent framework with test-time scaling for zero-shot composed image retrieval

method.training_loop: Multi-view worker agents extract priors, IR-Manager fuses via intent routing, DE-Manager performs tournament-style test-time scaling with experience-evolved reasoning policy distillation
method.data_source: Offline reasoning-aware sandbox with GRPO-style rollouts for experience distillation
key_components: Intent-aware Prior Routing
Multi-view Perception Workers
Reasoning Policy Distillation
Tournament-based Test-Time Scaling
Experience Self-evolution

2605.22478.novelty: First to introduce experience-driven self-evolution and test-time scaling into ZS-CIR via hierarchical multi-agent architecture with training-free reasoning policy distillation

on_policy_mechanism.evidence_quote: cannot find on-policy evidence

opd_classification.reasoning: This paper addresses zero-shot composed image retrieval using multi-agent test-time scaling, not on-policy distillation of language models.

key_findings: PDF achieves best results on 35 out of 38 reported metrics (92.1%) across CIRR, CIRCO, and FashionIQ
On CIRCO ViT-B/32, PDF improves mAP@5 by 45.47% over the strongest agentic baseline XR
Full model with deliberation achieves 23.76% relative improvement on FashionIQ R@10 and 58.94% on CIRCO mAP@5 over single-prior baseline
2605.22478.ablations_summary: Multi-view priors progressively improve performance; IPR outperforms average and static fusion; L=2 deliberation depth is optimal; experience guidance consistently helps; K=50 is the optimal candidate pool size balancing cost and accuracy

Relies on GPT-4o-mini API for LLM invocations

K>50 introduces contextual degradation and attention drift
